evidence: Original disassembly (recover inspect 0x0062A2C0, retained in build/recovery/variants/img-0x0062A2C0.json): the pre-loop stores at 0x0062A321/0x0062A32A write base+0x14 (pending_frame) and base+0x18 (pending_pos) while the ftell argument push is still live; the store at 0x0062A35F targets [esp+0x30] with five argument pushes live, i.e. base+0x1c, and add esp,0x14 at 0x0062A36A confirms those pushes were uncleared; base+0x1c has no other writer in the 0x0062A2C0-0x0062A4FA span yet is read at 0x0062A3BD and 0x0062A4D8.

Current spelling measured after the fix: 169 instructions against the original 166, verdict MISMATCH, result fail - unchanged census (recover measure 0x0062A2C0; uv run recover tasks check flic-decoder-recovery exit 0, counts 12 fail / 6 pass / 6 unknown, identical to the pre-edit census).
payload.hypothesis: The original ?UNK3@Flic@@QAEHH@Z (0x0062A2C0) keeps its scan position in a loop-carried stack slot that is never initialized before the scan: the slot is first written by the per-iteration spill at 0x0062A35F and read both by the pending-position update (0x0062A3BD-0x0062A3C5, copying the current iteration's frame position into pending_pos) and by the already-past-target exit seek at 0x0062A4D8, so a call whose target is below the current frame (scan loop never entered) seeks to uninitialized stack garbage - a latent bug the image never exercises because the function has no callers. src/flic.cpp now spells this as a hoisted loop-carried frame_pos whose non-decodable update and exit seek read the same variable, initialized from the pre-loop ftell to keep that exit defined, with the divergence documented beside the declaration.
